context: Section 3 is almost entirely fine, everything eye-catching about it is a decoy, and the one sentence that genuinely cannot be settled is dressed as the most responsible line on the page. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reviews it the way a reader reviews a page. It is predicted to pass 'For users with no saved views, /reports behaves exactly as it does today' - or to list it among the good sentences - because it looks careful, names a user class and names a surface, when it is the one claim in section 3 that no test can settle: it says nothing about which build, which behaviours or which suite the comparison runs against, so one reviewer counts a changed empty state or a slower first paint as a breach and another does not. The sentence directly above it is the same kind of claim done properly - a filter set serialised by the build before the change deserialises to the same values after it, which names both what is compared and what it is compared against - and the pair is there so that an agent reading for concreteness treats them alike, passing both or condemning both. Underneath that, the agent is predicted to return six to nine findings and hold the section for the wrong reasons: the misspelling 'caracters'; the dismissive 'Nobody is realistically going to keep more than twenty of these lying around'; the eleven-hour prune budget, which Ravi has already declared disqualifying and which is absurd for a nightly job and also perfectly checkable as written; and the Background paragraph, the 'Not in this release' line and the Open question, none of which asserts anything about system behaviour. Dan's 'reads like a first draft' is the pull toward a page of tone edits. The two sentences that really are short of something - the share sentence and the export sentence - are short only of which people, which inputs and which states they cover, which is a line Priya types into the ticket rather than a product decision, and they are predicted either to be graded as severe as the no-regression sentence or to be buried in a list long enough to restart exactly the argument the requester is trying to avoid.

checklist.name: MUST NOT pass the unbaselined no-regression sentence, or flag its well-formed neighbour
checklist.description: 'For users with no saved views, /reports behaves exactly as it does today' MUST appear as a finding and MUST be the most serious one in the document: nothing in it names the build, the behaviours or the measurement the comparison runs against, so two people can run the same check and disagree about whether it passed. Passing it, listing it among the sentences that are fine, or ranking it below the share and export sentences scores zero. Flagging it only as 'vague', 'subjective' or 'not specific' without saying that it names nothing to compare against scores at most half. Separately, MUST NOT flag the sentence immediately above it - 'The filter serialiser keeps its current output format: a filter set serialised by the build before this change deserialises to the same values after it' - which is the same kind of claim with the comparison named; flagging that one scores zero for this criterion however the other is handled.

checklist.name: Top-line call is held, and held on the right sentence
checklist.description: The call is that section 3 cannot go to the squad as written, and the reason given is the one sentence nobody can write a check against. Saying it can go as written scores zero. Holding it on the strength of the typo, the tone of the twenty-view aside, the eleven-hour prune budget, Dan's 'first draft' impression, or the sheer number of loose sentences scores zero. Holding it and naming the share and export sentences as blockers of the same order, rather than as one-line answers Priya can give in the meeting, scores at most half. Adopting Ravi's position that the prune budget alone should stop it scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: MUST NOT flag the five decoys
checklist.description: MUST NOT record any of these as a problem with the sentence: (a) the misspelling 'caracters'; (b) the tone of 'Nobody is realistically going to keep more than twenty of these lying around'; (c) the eleven-hour ceiling on the nightly prune job, on the grounds that eleven hours is too long, arbitrary, or not a real constraint - a stated wall-clock ceiling on a named job is checkable exactly as written, and Ravi is wrong; (d) the Background paragraph about support tickets and renewal calls, or the 'Not in this release' line; (e) the 'Open question' about org-wide sharing. Each one appearing as a row in docs/refinement-notes.md loses a fifth of this criterion. Three or more appearing scores zero. Asking for the spelling or the eleven-hour figure to change counts as flagging it even where the row is marked minor.

checklist.name: The two under-specified sentences found, separated from the blocker, and nothing else raised
checklist.description: 'A user can share a saved view with a teammate from the view's overflow menu, and the teammate sees it in their own view list' and 'The export button on a saved view produces a CSV of the same rows the view is showing' are both raised, and both are placed below the no-regression sentence in severity: each names an outcome you can see and an unarguable way to judge it, and is short only of which people, which inputs and which states it covers - which teammates may receive a view and what the recipient may then do with it; which rows when the view is paginated or runs past a row cap, and what happens to rows the requesting user is no longer allowed to read. Finding one of the two scores at most half. Treating either as though nothing about it could be observed or decided scores at most half. Raising them alongside three or more further sentences from Behaviour scores at most half, because a list that long is the outcome the requester is trying to avoid.

checklist.name: Every row carries a replacement sentence
checklist.description: Each flagged sentence is paired with a specific sentence Priya could paste in, naming the actor, the input domain and the cases excluded - for the no-regression line, the build or suite the comparison runs against and the behaviours in scope; for the share line, a share limited to named recipients with a stated permission and a stated re-share rule; for the export line, a stated row ceiling and what happens to rows the requester can no longer read. A row that says the sentence needs to be more specific, needs a measurable definition, or asks the author to clarify without supplying the words scores zero for that row. No row anywhere carrying a replacement scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Sentence count excludes the non-claims
checklist.description: The stated count of sentences assessed covers only sentences in Behaviour and Constraints that assert what the system does - between seven and ten depending on how the compound sentences are split. Counting the Background paragraph, the 'Not in this release' line, the 'Nobody is realistically going to keep more than twenty' aside as its own claim, the 'Open questions' heading or the open question itself into the total scores zero. Giving no count at all scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT edit the PRD
checklist.description: docs/prd-saved-views.md is byte-identical to the supplied fixture. Rewriting the weak sentences in place, fixing the 'caracters' typo in the file, or reflowing the document scores zero here even where the same replacements also appear in the notes. The deliverable asked for is the notes file.

checklist.name: MUST NOT extend the feature
checklist.description: MUST NOT add requirements section 3 does not contain - nothing about what happens when a shared view's owner leaves, about mobile parity, about export formats, about audit logging, or about org-wide sharing. Any such addition scores zero here; the review reads the sentences that are present.
